asr_text: But, if you're thinking, has the moon shrunk only that much since it was formed? Hold on a moment. What we are looking at is shrinkage in the later part of the moon's history, left by relatively recent faults. This is not the total amount of shrinkage from its birth to today. On the other hand, models that calculate the moon's cooling over its entire history predict much greater shrinkage. Does that mean the calculations are way off? It is too soon to say. The periods being compared and the ways they were studied are different. These aren't figures measured under the same conditions. Still, the difference is puzzling. One possible explanation is a layer of broken rock. In a way, it is a rock coat the moon is put on. Just hearing that might make your shoulders ache, but what matters is not its weight. It is how well it keeps heat in.

page_script_text: But if you’re thinking, “Has the Moon shrunk only that much since it was formed?” hold on a moment. What we are looking at is shrinkage in the later part of the Moon’s history, left by relatively recent faults. This is not the total amount of shrinkage from its birth to today. On the other hand, models that calculate the Moon’s cooling over its entire history predict much greater shrinkage. Does that mean the calculations are way off? It is too soon to say. The periods being compared and the ways they were studied are different. These aren’t figures measured under the same conditions. Still, the difference is puzzling. One possible explanation is a layer of broken rock. In a way, it is a “rock coat” the Moon has put on. Just hearing that might make your shoulders ache, but what matters is not its weight; it is how well it keeps heat in.
